abstract: This article presents a novel four-state refractive index (RI) sensor based on distinct phases of palladium (Pd) and vanadium dioxide (VO$_2$), controlled by orthogonal thermal and chemical stimuli. This is a numerical, simulation-only study: all results are obtained from two-dimensional finite-element method (FEM) simulations. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first reported multi-state reconfigurable RI sensor tuned by external control. VO$_2$ serves as a phase change material (PCM) offering two thermally switchable phases with highly contrasting optical properties, while the hydrogen absorption property of Pd provides two additional phases. Combining these, four operational states are realized: (i) $α$-Pd/low-$T$ VO$_2$; (ii) $β$-PdH$_x$/low-$T$ VO$_2$; (iii) $α$-Pd/high-$T$ VO$_2$; and (iv) $β$-PdH$_x$/high-$T$ VO$_2$. Thermal crosstalk between Pd and VO$_2$ is mitigated through tungsten (W) doping of VO$_2$. This work further introduces conditional state sensitivity (CSS), a novel figure of merit quantifying the optical contrast between each state transition. The proposed sensor achieves a peak sensitivity of 2871 nm/RIU for the undoped reference configuration and 2798 nm/RIU for the practical W-doped device, together with a peak CSS of 16,872 nm/RIU, establishing it as a multi-state reconfigurable platform with reduced thermal crosstalk and potential applications in industrial safety monitoring and optical logic gates.
